rows.question: can the boundary read the identity the TLS handshake proved?

probes.observed: real TLS handshake: the server's getpeercert produced SPKI sha256:95b711837740b5ff81ee02f48c3a5c09e99606e5bad75c4f28702990a540de90
the SPKI fingerprint is computed from the public key, so reissuing a certificate for the same key keeps the identity and a new key never inherits an old one

limits: the drill reads the certificate from a socketpair handshake; whether the deployed server exposes it to the application depends on the terminator (see agent_identity.peer_certificate)

limits: The SPKI fingerprint is the identity. A machine that can export its key is that machine to this platform; the private key is the credential and hardware-backed keys are the deployment's choice.
The registry is a deployment file. Who may write it is a control the platform does not own — that is the same trust the certificate authority already has.

Whether the TLS server in front of the API exposes its peer certificate to the application is a terminator property; the drill proves the application half and names the dependency rather than assuming it.
